notes: Google URL Inspection is readonly and does not request recrawling. Same-day inspection and HTML evidence reused where possible.

Missing summaries and transient source failures replaced by independently written, identity-bound summaries; the Goines author biography and Nescio book excerpt are replaced by summaries of the books.
Existing canonicals, edition identities, robots policy, database records, ratings and source-attributed descriptions on the other 273 pages remain unchanged.

Automatic Production SEO Monitoring disabled at the owner’s request and its scheduled trigger removed. The URL inventory remains available for manual use. One bounded post-release HTML verification; only representative browser checks load images.
No claim of guaranteed indexing, comprehensive sitewide ranking or measured billing reduction.

pages.beforeMetaDescription: Rode sneeuw in december van Simone van der Vlugt, voor het eerst verschenen in 2012. Bekijk boekinformatie en de beoordelingsstatus op LumiScore.
pages.text:
In het zestiende-eeuwse Leiden wordt een katholiek meisje verliefd op een jonge lutherse arts. Haar vader verzet zich tegen die relatie en onterft haar. Na hun huwelijk vertrekt het paar naar Breda, waar hun leven verbonden raakt met de aanhang van Willem van Oranje.

Simone van der Vlugt plaatst een liefdesverhaal in een samenleving waarin geloof ook bepaalt bij wie je hoort en op wie je kunt vertrouwen. De botsing tussen familieverwachtingen en een eigen keuze krijgt zo een politieke en religieuze achtergrond.

pages.author: John Grisham

sourceEvidence.method: Original prose checked against publisher, author or catalogue evidence. Bound to the production title, author, ISBN and language; work-level sources do not establish edition-specific extras.

pages.beforeMetaDescription: Gray Mountain by John Grisham, first published in 2014. View book information and its LumiScore rating status.
pages.text:
The financial crisis interrupts Samantha Kofer’s career at a large New York law firm. Hoping eventually to return, she accepts unpaid work at a legal aid clinic in a small Virginia town. Her new clients introduce her to a world far removed from Wall Street.

Coal mining lies at the centre of disputes over livelihoods, land and power. As Samantha becomes involved in local litigation, the danger extends beyond the courtroom. John Grisham follows a lawyer learning how much a community can conceal and what it may cost to challenge it.

pages.beforeSynopsis: For 23 years of his young life, Goines lived in the dark, despair-ridden world of the junkie. It started while he was doing military service in Korea, and ended when he was murdered in a drugs deal at the age of 39.
pages.beforeMetaDescription: Dopefiend by Donald Goines, first published in 1991. View book information and its LumiScore rating status.
pages.text:
Teddy and Terry begin their relationship with the prospect of a shared future. Teddy’s heroin use initially appears to be one part of his life, but when Terry also begins using, addiction increasingly determines their decisions and circumstances.

Donald Goines follows the damage to their relationship and the narrowing of their world. The novel draws on his experience of addiction to portray dependence, desperation and the shrinking choices available to its characters.

Grover discovers two young half-bloods and calls Percy Jackson for help. The rescue draws Percy and his friends into a new threat connected to Kronos. Meanwhile, Artemis has disappeared while tracking a monster whose power could endanger Olympus.

Working with the Hunters of Artemis, the demigods have little time to find the goddess and understand what she was pursuing. This third Percy Jackson adventure combines a rescue mission with the danger foretold in a prophecy about a Titan’s curse.

pages.text:
Ezeulu is the chief priest of Ulu, the deity worshipped by the villages of Umuaro. His authority faces pressure both from people within his community and from the British colonial administration. He sees himself as a guardian of religious order, but his judgement is also shaped by pride and personal ambition.

Chinua Achebe explores the tension between serving a community and trying to control it. The novel follows a struggle over belief and leadership in a society whose political and religious relationships are being changed by colonial power.

pages.title: Fooled by Randomness
pages.author: Nassim Nicholas Taleb

sourceEvidence.method: Original prose checked against publisher, author or catalogue evidence. Bound to the production title, author, ISBN and language; work-level sources do not establish edition-specific extras.

pages.beforeMetaDescription: Fooled by Randomness by Nassim Nicholas Taleb, first published in 2001. View book information and its LumiScore rating status.
pages.text:
Nassim Nicholas Taleb asks how often success attributed to skill is actually a result of chance. Financial trading supplies many of his examples, but the argument extends to the stories people construct about achievement, failure and the apparent order of events.

Historical figures, fictional characters and observations from business illustrate the difficulty of recognising randomness while living through it. The book examines probability and judgement, questioning the confidence with which people explain the past or expect a successful method to keep working.

pages.text:
Ashley Cordova is found dead in Manhattan, and the official conclusion is suicide. Journalist Scott McGrath suspects there is more to discover. His investigation leads back to her father, a celebrated horror director whose long absence from public life has helped create a disturbing legend.

McGrath has already damaged his career by pursuing Cordova. With the help of two strangers, he returns to the filmmaker’s world, where reputation, family history and the unsettling force of the films become increasingly difficult to separate.

pages.text:
Christopher Banks heeft in het Engeland van de jaren dertig naam gemaakt als detective. Toch blijft juist een raadsel uit zijn eigen jeugd onopgelost: zijn ouders verdwenen in Shanghai toen hij nog een kind was. Zijn professionele succes heeft die onzekerheid niet weggenomen.

De roman beweegt tussen Londen en Shanghai en tussen onderzoek en herinnering. Kazuo Ishiguro volgt een man die naar zijn verleden terug wil keren, terwijl zijn behoefte aan antwoorden steeds sterker verweven raakt met de manier waarop hij dat verleden begrijpt.

pages.title: Liar's poker
pages.author: Michael Lewis

sourceEvidence.method: Original prose checked against publisher, author or catalogue evidence. Bound to the production title, author, ISBN and language; work-level sources do not establish edition-specific extras.

pages.beforeMetaDescription: Liar's poker by Michael Lewis, first published in 1989. View book information and its LumiScore rating status.
pages.text:
Michael Lewis recalls his passage from trainee to bond salesman at Salomon Brothers during the financial boom of the 1980s. The trading floor becomes a world with its own language, hierarchies and measures of success, where money and status are closely linked.

His account combines personal experience with a portrait of the firm’s competitive culture. Humour runs through the story, but so do questions about ambition, risk and the behaviour rewarded by an industry moving large sums of other people’s money.

Tracy Kidder follows a company’s effort to develop and bring a new computer to market. The technical problem is inseparable from the people doing the work: their ambitions, working relationships and willingness to keep pursuing a demanding project.

The account captures the pressure and culture of an industry moving quickly towards new possibilities. It approaches technological innovation through sustained attention to work in progress, showing the human effort behind a machine that might otherwise be understood only through its specifications.

pages.text:
Regan, the daughter of an actress living in Washington, D.C., undergoes changes that leave the adults around her struggling for an explanation. The possibility of demonic possession draws religious questions into their attempts to understand what is happening.

William Peter Blatty’s horror novel centres on the effort to save a child and the strain that effort places on those trying to help. Fear, doubt and belief meet in a story whose threat enters an ordinary household and resists its familiar explanations.

pages.author: Ryder Carroll

pages.sourceName: Ryder Carroll — The Bullet Journal Method
pages.text:
Ryder Carroll explains the thinking behind Bullet Journal, a paper-based approach to organising tasks and reflecting on priorities. The method brings practical planning together with regular attention to what matters, rather than treating every item on a list as equally important.

This book introduces the system through an overview and examples that readers can adapt to their own lives. Its focus is the relationship between recording activity, reviewing it and making more deliberate decisions about where to direct time and attention.

pages.text:
Florian en Isabella negeren het verbod van hun stiefvader en sluipen op een avond in 1876 een abdij binnen. Terwijl het orkest speelt, verschijnt er een donkere schaduw en begint het gebouw uiteen te vallen. De kinderen moeten zich tussen de brokstukken in veiligheid brengen.

Hun ontsnapping is het begin van een nieuwe dreiging: het Onnoembare heeft het op Isabella gemunt. Paul van Loon vertelt in dit griezelavontuur over de gebeurtenissen die voorafgaan aan de gelijknamige Efteling-attractie, met een raadsel rond de kracht die de kinderen achtervolgt.

pages.title: Museum van onvoorwaardelijke overgave
pages.author: Dubravka Ugrešić

sourceEvidence.sourceName: Nijgh & Van Ditmar — Museum van onvoorwaardelijke overgave

pages.sourceName: Nijgh & Van Ditmar — Museum van onvoorwaardelijke overgave
pages.text:
Dubravka Ugrešić brengt herinneringen samen aan een wereld die door oorlog en ballingschap onbereikbaar is geworden. Gesprekken met haar moeder in Zagreb, persoonlijke overpeinzingen en losse indrukken krijgen een plaats naast citaten en beelden.

De onderdelen vormen geen eenvoudige, doorlopende levensgeschiedenis. Ze werken als de foto’s van een album waarin verbanden ontstaan tussen het persoonlijke leven en het voormalige Joegoslavië. Het boek onderzoekt wat herinneringen bewaren wanneer de vertrouwde omgeving verdwijnt en een nieuw bestaan elders begint.

pages.author: Chika Unigwe

sourceEvidence.sourceName: Bureau ISBN / De Bezige Bij — Fata Morgana

pages.text:
Vier Afrikaanse vrouwen vertrekken met de verwachting elders een beter leven op te bouwen. Via dezelfde mensensmokkelaar komen zij in Antwerpen terecht, waar zij in de prostitutie belanden. Wanneer Sisi sterft, worden de anderen gedwongen opnieuw naar hun eigen geschiedenis te kijken.

Chika Unigwe brengt hun verschillende levens samen rond de Vingerlingstraat. De roman onderzoekt de afstand tussen de toekomst waarop de vrouwen hoopten en hun dagelijkse werkelijkheid, maar ook de mogelijkheden om onder moeilijke omstandigheden overeind te blijven.

pages.title: Larung
pages.author: Ayu Utami

pages.text:
Ayu Utami verbindt de levens van Saman, Yasmin, Laila en hun vrienden met de politieke verhoudingen in Indonesië onder Soeharto. De massamoorden van 1965 blijven doorwerken in een samenleving waarin verzet gevaarlijk is en de militaire regering haar macht beschermt.

Verschillende personages en verhaallijnen laten zien hoe persoonlijke verlangens naast angst, onderdrukking en politieke betrokkenheid bestaan. Larung zet de wereld van Saman voort en plaatst intieme ervaringen binnen een geschiedenis van geweld die niet voorbij is.

pages.author: Dubravka Ugrešić

pages.sourceName: Christian Bourgois — Le Ministère de la douleur
pages.text:
Na haar vlucht uit het voormalige Joegoslavië geeft Tanja literatuuronderwijs aan de Universiteit van Amsterdam. Ook haar studenten dragen ervaringen van oorlog en ontheemding met zich mee. In de lessen probeert zij via gedeelde herinneringen iets terug te vinden van het verdwenen land.

Die zoektocht brengt hen niet vanzelf dichter bij elkaar. Oude spanningen en verschillende manieren van omgaan met verlies komen opnieuw naar boven. Dubravka Ugrešić schrijft over ballingschap en de grenzen van een gemeenschappelijk verleden, met ironie en zwarte humor naast verdriet.

Nescio laat in Dichtertje, De uitvreter en Titaantjes zien hoe hoge verwachtingen botsen met een alledaags bestaan. Zijn personages verlangen naar vrijheid, schoonheid en een leven dat meer betekent dan werken en zich aanpassen, maar merken hoe moeilijk zulke verlangens standhouden.

De drie verhalen verbinden jeugdige idealen met de teleurstellingen van het ouder worden. Nescio schrijft met humor en melancholie over mensen die de wereld anders zouden willen zien, zonder hun tekortkomingen of hun kwetsbaarheid uit het oog te verliezen.

pages.author: Matthew Pearl

In Boston in 1868, unexplained disasters turn attention towards the new Massachusetts Institute of Technology. Ships lose control in the harbour, and another catastrophe strikes the city. As suspicion of scientific experimentation grows, the institution faces attacks from its rivals and the press.

A group of students begins a secret investigation, using the training that others fear. Matthew Pearl combines a historical mystery with the uncertain early life of an institution whose first graduating class must defend both its future and the city around it.

The book treats familiar refreshments as products of technology and as participants in cultural exchange. Changes in what people drink become a route into larger questions about how communities meet, economies develop and ideas travel.

pages.text:
Byung-Chul Han examines forms of power that work through people’s desires, emotions and sense of freedom. His critique of neoliberalism considers how digital technology and the collection of data can turn apparently voluntary activity into a means of control.

The essay connects philosophical arguments about power with questions about the psyche and contemporary communication. Han also considers alternatives to this organisation of life, asking what freedom and independent action might mean under conditions shaped by constant measurement.

Wole Soyinka recalls his childhood in Aké, a Yoruba community in western Nigeria, in the years surrounding the Second World War. The world of his Christian parents exists alongside the spiritual traditions introduced to him by his grandfather.

Family routines, books, adventures and the discoveries of a curious child give shape to the memoir. Soyinka approaches the adults and institutions around him through remembered impressions, bringing the sounds and sensations of childhood into a portrait of a particular place and time.

pages.text:
After challenging an Islamophobic teacher, Zayneb is suspended and travels to stay with her aunt in Doha. There she meets Adam, who is privately coming to terms with a diagnosis of multiple sclerosis while his family is still grieving his mother.

Both teenagers keep journals, but neither easily shares everything they are thinking. Their growing connection brings questions of faith, injustice, illness and family into a romance about the difference between the roles people perform and the experiences they keep hidden.

pages.text:
Gerald Durrell recounts an expedition to Cameroon undertaken with the ambition of establishing his own zoo. He and his wife gather a collection of mammals, birds and reptiles, encountering both animal personalities and the practical difficulties of caring for them.

Returning to Britain creates a different challenge: the animals need a home, and finding someone willing to accommodate them proves difficult. The memoir follows the disorderly beginnings of a long-held ambition through travel, observation and comic mishaps.

pages.text:
Sirius, the Dog Star, is condemned for a murder he did not commit and sent to Earth in the body of a dog. To escape his sentence, he must recover a dangerous object called the Zoi. His new form leaves him dependent on humans and vulnerable to their cruelty.

A girl offers him affection, but she cannot shield him from every threat. Meanwhile, someone is determined to prevent his search from succeeding. Diana Wynne Jones brings a cosmic mystery into the everyday uncertainties of a dog’s life.

pages.text:
Patrick Lencioni uses a leadership fable to examine why talented people can struggle to work together. The story introduces a model in which difficulties with trust, disagreement, commitment, accountability and shared results reinforce one another.

The practical discussion turns attention from individual ability to the habits of a group. It asks whether colleagues can admit mistakes, challenge ideas openly and follow through on decisions, presenting teamwork as a discipline that requires deliberate changes in behaviour.

pages.text:
Mark Miodownik examines the materials that make everyday objects possible. Metal, paper, ceramics and other familiar substances become starting points for explaining how structure, manufacturing and human ingenuity determine what things can do.

The book moves between ordinary possessions and ambitious technologies, connecting scientific properties with the history of design. Rather than treating the material world as a finished background to daily life, Miodownik shows how it has been understood, altered and put to new uses.

pages.author: Patricia Wallace

sourceEvidence.method: Existing attributed synopsis reviewed for relevance and retained.

pages.beforeSynopsis:
This timely volume explores the psychological aspects of cyberspace, a virtual world in which people from around the globe are acting and interacting in many new, unusual, and occasionally alarming ways.
Drawing on research in the social sciences, communications, business, and other fields, Patricia Wallace examines how the online environment can influence the way we behave, sometimes for the better, sometimes not.
Our own online behavior then becomes part of the Internet's psychological environment for others, creating opportunities for shaping the way this new territory for human interaction is unfolding.
Since the Internet--and our experience within it--is still young, we have a rare window of opportunity to influence the course of its development.
With a new preface that incorporates many of the changes online and in the field since the hardcover edition was published, the paperback edition of The Psychology of the Internet includes the latest coverage of e-commerce, workplace surveillance and datamining, all areas of recent intense public concern. Patricia M.
Wallace is Executive Director of the Center for Knowledge and Information Management at the Robert H. Smith School of Business, University of Maryland. She is author of an interactive psychology CD-ROM called PRISM and of the textbook Introduction to Psychology, Fourth Edition (with Jeffrey Goldstein). Dr.
Wallace is also the principal investigator on grants from the Annenberg Projects/Corporation for Public Broadcasting dealing with language learning through CD-ROMs and the Internet.

pages.beforeSynopsis:
"The larger-than-life journey of an 18-year-old college freshman who set out from his dorm room to track down Bill Gates, Lady Gaga, and dozens more of the world's most successful people to uncover how they broke through and launched their careers.
The Third Door takes readers on an unprecedented adventure--from hacking Warren Buffett's shareholders meeting to chasing Larry King through a grocery store to celebrating in a nightclub with Lady Gaga--as Alex Banayan travels from icon to icon, decoding their success.
After remarkable one-on-one interviews with Bill Gates, Maya Angelou, Steve Wozniak, Jane Goodall, Larry King, Jessica Alba, Pitbull, Tim Ferriss, Quincy Jones, and many more, Alex discovered the one key they have in common: they all took the Third Door. Life, business, success... it's just like a nightclub.
There are always three ways in. There's the First Door: the main entrance, where ninety-nine percent of people wait in line, hoping to get in. The Second Door: the VIP entrance, where the billionaires and celebrities slip through. But what no one tells you is that there is always, always... the Third Door.
It's the entrance where you have to jump out of line, run down the alley, bang on the door a hundred times, climb over the dumpster, crack open the window, sneak through the kitchen--there's always a way in.
Whether it's how Bill Gates sold his first piece of software or how Steven Spielberg became the youngest studio director in Hollywood history, they all took the Third Door"--

pages.beforeSynopsis:
Presents an assessment of Israel's state-sponsored assassination programs that evaluates the protective beliefs that are instituted into every Israeli citizen, the role of assassination in the state's history, and the ethical challenges of Israel's policies on targeted killings.
"The first definitive history of the Mossad, Shin Bet, and the IDF's targeted killing programs, from the man hailed by David Remnick as "arguably [Israel's] best investigative reporter." The Talmud says: "If someone comes to kill you, rise up and kill him first."
This instinct to take every measure, even the most aggressive, to defend the Jewish people is hardwired into Israel's DNA.
From the very beginning of its statehood in 1948, protecting the nation from harm has been the responsibility of its intelligence community and armed services, and there is one weapon in their vast arsenal that they have relied upon to thwart the most serious threats: Targeted assassinations have been used countless
times, on enemies large and small, sometimes in response to attacks against the Israeli people and sometimes preemptively.
In this page-turning, eye-opening book, journalist and military analyst Ronen Bergman offers a riveting inside account of the targeted killing programs--their successes, their failures, and the moral and political price exacted on the men and women who approved and carried out the missions.
Bergman has gained the exceedingly rare cooperation of many current and former members of the Israeli government, including Prime Ministers Shimon Peres, Ehud Barak, Ariel Sharon, and Benjamin Netanyahu, as well as high-level figures in the country's military and intelligence services: the IDF (Israel Defense Forces),
the Mossad (the world's most feared intelligence agency), Caesarea (a "Mossad within the Mossad" that carries out attacks on the highest-value targets), and the Shin Bet (an internal security service that implemented the largest targeted assassination campaign ever, in order to stop what had once appeared to be
unstoppable: suicide terrorism).
Including never-before-reported, behind-the-curtain accounts of key operations, and based on hundreds of on-the-record interviews and thousands of files to which Bergman has gotten exclusive access over his decades of reporting, Rise and Kill First brings us deep into the heart of Israel's most secret activities.
Bergman traces, from statehood to the present, the gripping events and thorny ethical questions underlying Israel's targeted killing campaign, which has shaped the Israeli nation, the Middle East, and the entire world."--Dust jacket.

pages.title: Give and take
pages.author: Adam Grant

sourceEvidence.method: Existing attributed synopsis reviewed for relevance and retained.

pages.beforeSynopsis:
For generations, we have focused on the individual drivers of success: passion, hard work, talent, and luck. But in today's dramatically reconfigured world, success is increasingly dependent on how we interact with others.
This book illuminates what effective networking, collaboration, influence, negotiation, and leadership skills have in common. The author examines the surprising forces that shape why some people rise to the top of the success ladder while others sink to the bottom.
In professional interactions, it turns out that most people operate as either takers, matchers, or givers. Whereas takers strive to get as much as possible from others and matchers aim to trade evenly, givers are the rare breed of people who contribute to others without expecting anything in return.
Using his own studies, the author reveals that these styles have a dramatic impact on success. Although some givers get exploited and burn out, the rest achieve extraordinary results across a wide range of industries.
Combining evidence with stories, this book shows how one of America's best networkers developed his connections; why the creative genius behind one of the most popular shows in television history toiled for years in anonymity; how a basketball executive responsible for multiple draft busts transformed his franchise
into a winner; and how we could have anticipated Enron's demise four years before the company collapsed, without ever looking at a single number.

pages.beforeSynopsis:
From one of our most perceptive commentators and winner of the National Book Award, a comprehensive look at the new world of globalization, the international system that, more than anything else, is shaping world affairs today. As the Foreign Affairs columnist forThe New York Times, Thomas L.
Friedman has traveled the globe, interviewing people from all walks of contemporary life: Brazilian peasants in the Amazon rain forest, new entrepreneurs in Indonesia, Islamic students in Teheran, and the financial wizards on Wall Street and in Silicon Valley.
Now Friedman has drawn on his years on the road to produce an engrossing and original look at globalization. Globalization, he argues, is not just a phenomenon and not just a passing trend.
It is the international system that replaced the Cold War system; the new, well-greased, interconnected system: Globalization is the integration of capital, technology, and information across national borders, in a way that is creating a single global market and, to some degreee, a global village.
Simply put, one can't possibly understand the morning news or one's own investments without some grasp of the system. Just one example: During the Cold War, we reached for the hot line between the White House and the Kremlin--a symbol that we were all divided but at least the two superpowers were in charge.
In the era of globalization, we reach for the Internet--a symbol that we are all connected but nobody is totally in charge. With vivid stories and a set of original terms and concepts, Friedman offers readers remarkable access to his unique understanding of this new world order, and shows us how to see this new system.
He dramatizes the conflict of "the Lexus and the olive tree"--the tension between the globalization system and ancient forces of culture, geography, tradition, and community.
He also details the powerful backlash that globalization produces among those who feel brutalized by it, and he spells out what we all need to do to keep the system in balance.
Finding the proper balance between the Lexus and the olive tree is the great drama of he globalization era, and the ultimate theme of Friedman's challenging, provocative book--essential reading for all who care about how the world really works.

A lifelong disability, or a naturally occurring form of cognitive difference akin to certain forms of genius? In truth, it is all of these things and more--and the future of our society depends on our understanding it.
WIRED reporter Steve Silberman unearths the secret history of autism, long suppressed by the same clinicians who became famous for discovering it, and finds surprising answers to the crucial question of why the number of diagnoses has soared in recent years.

A strikingly original, beautifully narrated history of Western architecture and the cultural transformations that it represents Concrete, marble, steel, brick: little else made by human hands seems as stable, as immutable, as a building. Yet the life of any structure is neither fixed nor timeless.
Outliving their original contexts and purposes, buildings are forced to adapt to each succeeding age. To survive, they must become shape-shifters.
In an inspired refashioning of architectural history, Edward Hollis recounts more than a dozen stories of such metamorphosis, highlighting the way in which even the most familiar structures all change over time into “something rich and strange.”

Remains of the Berlin Wall, meanwhile, which was once gleefully smashed and bulldozed, are now treated as precious relics. Altered layer by layer with each generation, buildings become eloquent chroniclers of the civilizations they’ve witnessed.

pages.beforeSynopsis:
Like many ambitious New York City teenagers, Craig Gilner sees entry into Manhattan’s Executive Pre-Professional High School as the ticket to his future.
Determined to succeed at life—which means getting into the right high school to get into the right college to get the right job—Craig studies night and day to ace the entrance exam, and does. That’s when things start to get crazy.
At his new school, Craig realizes that he isn't brilliant compared to the other kids; he’s just average, and maybe not even that. He soon sees his once-perfect future crumbling away. The stress becomes unbearable and Craig stops eating and sleeping—until, one night, he nearly kills himself.
Craig’s suicidal episode gets him checked into a mental hospital, where his new neighbors include a transsexual sex addict, a girl who has scarred her own face with scissors, and the self-elected President Armelio.
There, isolated from the crushing pressures of school and friends, Craig is finally able to confront the sources of his anxiety. Ned Vizzini, who himself spent time in a psychiatric hospital, has created a remarkably moving tale about the sometimes unexpected road to happiness.
For a novel about depression, it’s definitely a funny story.

pages.title: The Finisher
pages.author: David Baldacci

sourceEvidence.method: Existing attributed synopsis reviewed for relevance and retained.

pages.beforeSynopsis:
"Why would Quentin Herms flee into the Quag? There was nothing in the Quag except certain death. Vega Jane has never left the village of Wormwood. But this isn't unusual--nobody has ever left the village of Wormwood. At least not until Quentin Herms vanishes into the unknown.
Vega knows Quentin didn't just leave--he was chased. And he's left behind a very dangerous trail of clues that only she can decode. The Quag is a dark forest filled with terrifying beasts and bloodthirsty Outliers. But just as deadly are the threats that exist within the walls of Wormwood.
It is a place built on lies, where influential people are willing to kill to keep their secrets. Vega is determined to uncover the truth--but the closer she gets, the more she risks her life"--

pages.author: Alessandro Baricco

sourceEvidence.method: Existing attributed synopsis reviewed for relevance and retained.

pages.beforeSynopsis:
From the author of the international best-seller Silk, come s haunting, suspenseful tale of love and vengeance.
A handful of disparate lives converge at a remote seaside inn: a lovelorn professor, a renowned painter, an inscrutable seductress - and a beautiful young girl, fatally ill, brought to the sea by a desperate father's last hope.
An intricate web of destinies and associations begins to reveal itself, but it is not until the arrival of a mysterious sailor called Adams that the truth in all its dreamlike beauty and cruelty becomes clear.
Adams may furnish the key to the girl's salvation, but only the fulfillment of his obsessive secret purpose to answer murder with murder - can conclude the journey that has brought him from the ends of the ear.
Alternately playful and profoundly serious, Allesandro Baricco's new novel surges with the hypnotic power of the ocean sea. (front flap)

pages.beforeSynopsis:
New York Times bestseller and Newbery Honor Book! A gorgeously written, hopeful middle grade novel in verse about a young girl who must leave Syria to move to the United States, perfect for fans of Jason Reynolds and Aisha Saeed.
Jude never thought she’d be leaving her beloved older brother and father behind, all the way across the ocean in Syria. But when things in her hometown start becoming volatile, Jude and her mother are sent to live in Cincinnati with relatives. At first, everything in America seems too fast and too loud.
The American movies that Jude has always loved haven’t quite prepared her for starting school in the US—and her new label of “Middle Eastern,” an identity she’s never known before.
But this life also brings unexpected surprises—there are new friends, a whole new family, and a school musical that Jude might just try out for. Maybe America, too, is a place where Jude can be seen as she really is.
This lyrical, life-affirming story is about losing and finding home and, most importantly, finding yourself.

sourceEvidence.method: Existing attributed synopsis reviewed for relevance and retained.

pages.beforeSynopsis:
"When a mysterious young woman named Katie appears in the small North Carolina town of Southport, her sudden arrival raises questions about her past.
Beautiful yet self-effacing, Katie seems determined to avoid forming personal ties until a series of events draws her into two reluctant relationships: one with Alex, a widowed store owner with a kind heart and two young children; and another with her plainspoken single neighbor, Jo.
Despite her reservations, Katie slowly begins to let down her guard, putting down roots in the close-knit community and becoming increasingly attached to Alex and his family.
But even as Katie begins to fall in love, she struggles with the dark secret that still haunts and terrifies her-- a past that set her on a fearful, shattering journey across the country, to the sheltered oasis of Southport.
With Jo's empathic and stubborn support, Katie eventually realizes that she must choose between a life of transient safety and one of riskier rewards-- and that in the darkest hour, love is the only true safe haven"--from author's web site.

pages.beforeSynopsis:
Darius doesn't think he'll ever be enough, in America or in Iran. Hilarious and heartbreaking, this unforgettable debut introduces a brilliant new voice in contemporary YA. Winner of the William C. Morris Debut Award “Heartfelt, tender, and so utterly real. I’d live in this book forever if I could.”
—Becky Albertalli, award-winning author of Simon vs. the Homo Sapiens Agenda Darius Kellner speaks better Klingon than Farsi, and he knows more about Hobbit social cues than Persian ones. He’s a Fractional Persian—half, his mom’s side—and his first-ever trip to Iran is about to change his life.
Darius has never really fit in at home, and he’s sure things are going to be the same in Iran. His clinical depression doesn’t exactly help matters, and trying to explain his medication to his grandparents only makes things harder. Then Darius meets Sohrab, the boy next door, and everything changes.
Soon, they’re spending their days together, playing soccer, eating faludeh, and talking for hours on a secret rooftop overlooking the city’s skyline. Sohrab calls him Darioush—the original Persian version of his name—and Darius has never felt more like himself than he does now that he’s Darioush to Sohrab.
Adib Khorram’s brilliant debut is for anyone who’s ever felt not good enough—then met a friend who makes them feel so much better than okay.

pages.beforeSynopsis:
A wine connoisseur with an infallible palate and a sinister taste in wagers. A decrepit old man with a masterpiece tattooed on his back. A voracious adventuress, a gentle cuckold, and a garden sculpture that becomes an instrument of sadistic vengeance. Social climbers who climb a bit too quickly.
Philanderers whose deceptions are a trifle too ornate. Impeccable servants whose bland masks slip for one vertiginous instant.
In these deliciously nasty stories an internationally acclaimed practitioner of the short narrative works his own brand of black magic: tantalizing, amusing, and sometimes terrifying readers into a new sense of what lurks beneath the ordinary.
Included in Roald Dahl's Tales of the Unexpected are such notorious gems of the bizarre as "The Sound Machine," "Lamb to Slaughter," "Neck," and "The Landlady."

pages.beforeSynopsis:
This is the story of two boys, Dylan Ebdus and Mingus Rude. They live in Brooklyn and are friends and neighbours; but since Dylan is white and Mingus is black, their friendship is not simple.
This is the story of 1970s America, a time when the simplest decisions - what music you listen to, whether to speak to the kid in the seat next to you, whether to give up your lunch money - are laden with potential political, social and racial disaster.
This is also the story of 1990s America, when nobody cared anymore.
This is the story of what would happen if two teenaged boys obsessed with comic book heroes actually had superpowers: they would screw up their lives. --back cover

storedDescription.text: Elke Wiss onderzoekt waarom gesprekken zo gemakkelijk veranderen in pogingen om gelijk te krijgen. Met Socrates als voorbeeld beschrijft zij een andere houding: nieuwsgierig blijven, luisteren en onderzoeken wat de ander precies bedoelt. Het boek bespreekt hoe een vraag een gesprek kan openen en hoe aannames juist verdere uitwisseling kunnen verhinderen. Praktische oefeningen en filosofische achtergronden ondersteunen dat onderzoek. Wiss biedt geen vaste lijst die in iedere situatie werkt, maar een manier om bewuster vragen te leren stellen.

Het boek bespreekt hoe een vraag een gesprek kan openen en hoe aannames juist verdere uitwisseling kunnen verhinderen. Praktische oefeningen en filosofische achtergronden ondersteunen dat onderzoek. Wiss biedt geen vaste lijst die in iedere situatie werkt, maar een manier om bewuster vragen te leren stellen.

pages.title: De laatste Aedema
pages.author: Marjolijn van Heemstra

sourceEvidence.method: Existing attributed synopsis reviewed for relevance and retained.

pages.beforeSynopsis:
Op een dag krijgt Loina Aedema, telg uit een oud adellijk geslacht, te horen dat ze de laatste is in een lange lijn, dat haar familie met haar zal uitsterven. Toen Loina nog een baby was, kwamen haar ouders om het leven bij een verkeersongeluk.
Sindsdien woont ze bij haar grootvader op een zolderverdieping, te midden van stoffige familiestukken, aangestaard door de portretten van haar voorouders. Dan komt oom Samson met een opdracht, of Loina wil uitzoeken waar de kiem ligt van hun tragische familiegeschiedenis.
Het brengt haar op het spoor van haar overgrootmoeder, die zomaar, van de ene op de andere dag, verdween. En dan is daar nog de mysterieuze jongen Dawud, die zich plotseling aan haar opdringt. Een roman over afkomst, opvoeding, tradities en nieuwe waarden.
Een debuut met een actueel thema: is er nog een elite en kan die nog een rol van betekenis spelen in deze populistische tijden?0Marjolijn van Heemstra (1981) studeerde godsdienstwetenschappen, maakt theater en schrijft voor 'nrc.next' en 'Vrij Nederland'.

pages.title: De grote goede dingen
pages.author: Alma Mathijsen

sourceEvidence.method: Existing attributed synopsis reviewed for relevance and retained.

pages.beforeSynopsis:
"De jonge Mila levert zich over aan de grillen van Don, de oudere succesvolle violist en vriend van haar overleden vader. Don en haar vader vormden samen met Kapitein Blauwbaard en Herman in de jaren zestig een geniaal anarchistisch strijkkwartet. Nu heeft Don geen plezier meer in muziek en lijdt hij aan faalangst.
Mila past terwijl hij op tournee is op zijn huis. Als op een nacht een dierbaar instrument van haar vader wordt ontvreemd, dwingt Don haar mee te gaan om het te zoeken. Hun reis voert langs de oude vrienden. Mila leert het verleden van haar vader kennen op een nietsontziende manier.
Het ideaalbeeld dat ze van hem heeft gevormd breekt Don stelselmatig af. Mila groeit naar acceptatie van verlies in de confrontatie met de complexe persoonlijkheid die haar vader was. Mathijsen geeft een indringend beeld van het kunstenaarsleven in de jaren zestig en de nasleep ervan twintig jaar later.
In dit boek verbindt de schrijfster twee tijdperken met elkaar en dringt door tot de kern van wat verbeelding doet met mensen."

storedDescription.text: Maryse Condé geeft een eigen stem aan Tituba, de tot slaaf gemaakte vrouw die tijdens de heksenvervolgingen in Salem werd beschuldigd. Vanuit de schaarse historische gegevens verbeeldt zij een uitgebreider leven, met een jeugd, relaties en kennis van rituelen en genezing. Tituba's ervaringen brengen slavernij, racisme en religieuze vervolging bij elkaar. De roman behandelt haar niet alleen als een naam uit een procesverslag, maar als iemand die zelf vertelt. Het is nadrukkelijk fictie rond een historische figuur, geen gedocumenteerde levensbeschrijving.

pages.title: De oorlog heeft geen vrouwengezicht
pages.author: Светлана Алексиевич

sourceEvidence.method: Existing attributed synopsis reviewed for relevance and retained.

pages.beforeSynopsis:
Tijdens de Tweede Wereldoorlog vochten ongeveer een miljoen vrouwen in het Rode Leger, maar hun verhaal is nooit verteld. In De oorlog heeft geen vrouwengezicht verzamelde Svetlana Alexijevitsj de herinneringen van honderden van hen die scherpschutter waren, tanks bestuurden of in veldhospitaals werkten.
Hun verhaal is niet het verhaal van strijd alleen, maar dat van mensen in oorlog: wat gebeurde er met hen, hoe werden ze door de oorlog veranderd? Hoe was het om te leren te doden?
Samen vertellen ze het niet-heroïsche verhaal van de oorlog, dat ontbreekt in eerdere getuigenissen van veteranen. Alexijevitsj publiceerde haar boek in 1985, maar heeft het in 2002 compleet herzien, waarbij ze gedeelten heeft kunnen toevoegen die oorspronkelijk ten prooi waren gevallen aan de Sovjet-censuur.

pages.beforeSynopsis:
Fantasia 16 is het nieuwste deel van Fantasia - Verschenen in oktober 2021 Kersverse keizerin Alina heeft het oude imperium nieuw leven ingeblazen met haar harmonieuze manier van regeren. Maar helaas duurt deze vredige periode niet lang; een nieuwe dreiging brengt het magische gebied meteen alweer uit zijn evenwicht.
Want in een vergeten rijk heeft het Leger der Onzichtbaren in het geheim een nieuwe aanval beraamd en nu raast er iets afschrikwekkends over Fantasia, dat alles en iedereen op zijn pad van kleur doet verschieten en in gevaar brengt.
De Ridder zonder Vrees of Blaam, oftewel Geronimo, wordt ingeschakeld om het samen met Alina, haar trouwe drakentemmer en nog twee bijzondere bondgenoten op te nemen tegen deze venijnige vijand. Lukt het ze hem uit de weg te ruimen voordat Fantasia voor altijd van al zijn schitterende kleuren en geuren beroofd is?

Onder de opgenomen teksten staat ook zijn eerste betaalde verhaal, dat aanvankelijk onder een andere titel verscheen.
Het boek laat daarmee een vroeg gedeelte van zijn schrijverschap zien. De ervaringen uit de luchtvaart vormen een gezamenlijke achtergrond, zonder dat de verhalen daardoor als letterlijke memoires moeten worden gelezen.

sourceEvidence.method: Existing attributed synopsis reviewed for relevance and retained.

pages.beforeSynopsis:
Evil has been defeated. The war has just begun.
They did the impossible, deposing the godlike being whose brutal rule had lasted a thousand years. Now Vin, the street urchin who has grown into the most powerful Mistborn in the land, and Elend Venture, the idealistic young nobleman who loves her,must build a healthy new society in the ashes of an empire.
They have barely begun when three separate armies attack. As the siege tightens, an ancient legend seems to offer a glimmer of hope. But even if it really exists, no one knows where to find the Well of Ascension or what manner of power it bestows.
It may just be that killing the Lord Ruler was the easy part. Surviving the aftermath of his fall is going to be the real challenge.
"A great epic fantasy... Fans of Terry Goodkind and Terry Brooks will find THE WELL OF ASCENSION fulfilling, satisfying, and incredibly exciting. -SFRev

pages.beforeSynopsis:
Ambitie motiveert hem. Competitie drijft hem. Maar macht kent een prijs.
Het is de ochtend van de boeteceremonie waarmee de tiende jaarlijkse Hongerspelen worden ingeluid. In het Capitool bereidt de achttienjarige Coriolanus Snow zich voor op zijn enige kans op roem en succes, als mentor in de spelen.
Zijn ooit zo machtige familie heeft het moeilijk en hoe het hun verder zal vergaan, hangt af van Coriolanus' prestaties. Hij moet charmanter, slimmer en geraffineerder te werk gaan dan zijn medestudenten en zijn tribuut naar de overwinning helpen.
Maar het zit hem niet mee. Hij krijgt de vernederende opdracht om mentor te zijn van de vrouwelijke tribuut uit district 12, het laagste van het laagste. Vanaf nu zijn Coriolanus en zijn tribuut verbonden door hun lot: iedere keuze die hij maakt kan leiden tot gunst of mislukking, zege of ondergang.
In de arena zal worden gevochten tot de dood. Buiten de arena begint Coriolanus mee te leven met zijn tribuut… en moet hij kiezen wat hij belangrijker vindt: de regels blijven volgen of doen wat nodig is om te overleven.

pages.beforeSynopsis:
CAMERON, ETHAN AND PHILIP were all troubled young boys who were rescued and adopted at difficult periods in their lives by the extraordinary couple, Raymond and Stella Quinn.
Now grown and living on their own, the Quinn brothers must return to the family home on the Maryland shore, to honour their father's last request. Sea Swept is Cameron's story.
Cameron has lived the reckless life of a daredevil since leaving the quiet community of Chesapeake Bay. He likes fast cars, fast boats and fast women. But when his dying father calls him home to care for Seth, a troubled young boy not unlike Cameron once was, his life changes overnight.
After years of independence, Cameron has to learn to live with his brothers once again, while he struggles with taking care of a difficult teenager. Old rivalries and new resentments flare between Cameron and his brothers but they have to try and set aside their differences for sake.
Only fate is in the hands of a tough but beautifur social worker. She alone has the power to bring the Quinns together — or tear them apart... --front flap

pages.title: Finding Me
pages.author: Viola Davis

sourceEvidence.method: Existing attributed synopsis reviewed for relevance and retained.

pages.beforeSynopsis:
In my book, you will meet a little girl named Viola who ran from her past until she made a life-changing decision to stop running forever. This is my story, from a crumbling apartment in Central Falls, Rhode Island, to the stage in New York City, and beyond.
This is the path I took to finding my purpose but also my voice in a world that didn't always see me. As I wrote Finding Me, my eyes were open to the truth of how our stories are often not given close examination. We are forced to reinvent them to fit into a crazy, competitive, judgmental world.
So I wrote this for anyone running through life untethered, desperate and clawing their way through murky memories, trying to get to some form of self-love. For anyone who needs reminding that a life worth living can only be born from radical honesty and the courage to shed facades and be . . . you.
Finding Me is a deep reflection, a promise, and a love letter of sorts to self. My hope is that my story will inspire you to light up your own life with creative expression and rediscover who you were before the world put a label on you.

Nog een kinderboek waarin een onverwachte vriendschap draait om welkom zijn en elkaar beschermen.
Montgomery volgt een weesmeisje dat een plaats probeert te vinden binnen een onverwacht gezin.
Vergelijk het vertrouwde landschap van pratende dieren met Alice’ veel onvoorspelbaardere ontmoetingen.
Grahame geeft de sprekende dieren een rustiger rivierlandschap en legt de nadruk op hun vriendschappen.
Lees verder bij Mulisch over hoe één gebeurtenis lang doorwerkt in vragen over schuld en verantwoordelijkheid.
Mulisch verbreedt de verhouding tussen keuzes, geschiedenis en verantwoordelijkheid tot een verhaal met een hemels perspectief.
Vergelijk twee romans waarin een man steeds meer gaat leven binnen een verhaal waarvan hij de waarheid niet zeker kent.
Koch laat vermoedens over ontrouw verstrengeld raken met het privéleven en publieke verleden van een burgemeester.
Vergelijk een man die aan zijn familierol wil ontsnappen met een vrouw die onderzoekt hoe zulke rollen haar leven bepalen.
Verhulst kiest een ironische ontsnappingspoging als ingang tot de verwachtingen die een familie iemand oplegt.
Vergelijk twee historische liefdesverhalen waarin een verschil in geloof een breuk met de familie veroorzaakt.
Hertmans volgt een veel vroegere vlucht, vanuit de elfde eeuw, en verbindt het verhaal met historisch onderzoek.
Nog een familieverhaal waarin economische onzekerheid en een ingrijpende verandering de onderlinge verhoudingen op de proef stellen.
Isik kiest het perspectief van een jongen in Oost-Turkije, waar familiegeschiedenis en een ongeluk het dagelijks leven veranderen.
Lees verder bij Noort over een succesvol ogend vrouwenleven dat door relatieproblemen zijn zekerheid verliest.
Noort laat de ontregeling hier samenkomen rond een nieuwe kliniek, een huwelijk en een uit de hand lopende verbouwing.
Vergelijk twee romans waarin ervaringen uit het gezin van vroeger blijven doorwerken in volwassen relaties.
Verhoef concentreert de doorwerking van een moeilijke jeugd op een huwelijk en een verhouding die steeds minder houvast bieden.
